Maria K: quick idea — what if we introduce a "surface mask" on client-facing version headers so we don't leak variant internals during rollouts?
Sam H: can you sketch what "surface mask" means in practice?
Maria K: yeah — instead of exposing full pin or hash we emit a stable token + rollout tag. e.g. `X-Model-Version: v=3.2;cohort=canary-17;token=XXX` where token is opaque to clients.
Lee C: opaque token sounds fine, but how do we correlate in logs/trace for debugging?
Maria K: server side we keep mapping token -> full metadata. Traces have internal fields `model.pin` and `model.hash` only in internal logs — not returned to caller.
Ada P: concern: some customers depend on raw version header for reproducibility. Masking could break customer debug flows.
Mason R: could offer an opt-in header: `X-Model-Version-Raw` available only for Dedicated/Private with a flag. Hosted customers get masked by default.
Sam H: +1 for opt-in. Also need a migration plan for SDKs that parse versions. Might cause metrics spikes if suddenly missing fields.
Maria K: proposal: rollout plan = (1) add masked header and `X-Model-Version-Flags` that lists features, (2) document SDK change, (3) enable opt-in raw header for tenants that request it, (4) default mask after 30 days unless opted-in.
Lee C: telemetry: we should emit a stable metric label for `serving_variant` derived from token -> variant mapping to preserve cardinality control. Avoid leaking hash in metrics labels.
Ada P: agree. Also add a fallback for cases when token mapping is evicted — return `token=unknown` and increment `variant.resolve_miss` metric.
Infra Bot: deploy-checks ok: config flag `features.surface_mask` gate added to rollout-service, requires migration of trace sanitizer.
Mason R: ops note — need backfill script to annotate traces from last 90d with token mapping when we flip on mask. Otherwise debugging historical issues harder.
Sam H: question on rollout metadata schema: do we add `masked_token` as a first-class field in the manifest? or compute it at publish-time?
Maria K: compute at publish-time and store mapping in tenancy-aware store. Schema stays minimal: manifest keeps `variants[]` with IDs and fingerprints; masking is a separate mapping layer.
Lee C: sounds cleaner. But edge case: canary -> scaled -> promoted to stable with new fingerprint; token should follow lifecycle so we can trace promotion.
Maria K: yes token generation must be stable across promotion if the variant identity persists; otherwise generate new token and emit `promotion_event` metric.
Ada P: privacy/regulatory note: ensure tokens do not embed tenant ids or sensitive info. Use HMAC with service key + variant id salt.
Sam H: nice. Who wants to draft a short RFC? I can start a one-pager with examples and metrics semantics.
Maria K: I'll add a section on SDK compatibility and an opt-in request flow for Dedicated/Private.
Mason R: I'll own the backfill/tracing job and infra gating.
Lee C: can someone add a tiny example snippet for ops playbook? e.g. how to interpret `token=unknown` and next steps.
Maria K: sure — quick snippet: ```
# ops checklist when token=unknown
1) check `variant.resolve_miss` metric for spikes
2) query token-mapping-store by request trace id
3) if mapping missing, run backfill job for trace window
```
Sam H: perfect. Ok let's sync once RFC draft is up. :thumbsup:
Maria K: thanks everyone — ping me if you want to be on the RFC reviewers list.
Infra Bot: noted — reviewers requested: Maria K, Sam H, Lee C, Ada P, Mason R.
